source.quote:
The present tense verb is composed of three parts: present verbal stem, connecting vowel, and primary personal ending.
In the indicative mood, if the personal ending begins with mu or nu, the connecting vowel is omicron; otherwise the connecting vowel is epsilon.
A verb must agree with its subject in person and number.
The present active tense uses the primary active endings: ω, εις, ει, ομεν, ετε, ουσι(ν). The real personal endings are -, ς, ι, μεν, τε, νσι.
A movable nu can be added to the third person plural personal ending.
If the subject is "we" (ημείς) the verb would end in ομεν.
λύομεν means We are loosing. λύετε means You are loosing. λύουσι(ν) means They are loosing.
